sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Caswallawn is a hero of Wales. He is also called Casswallon. The form Caswallan fab Beli Mawr marks him as the son of Beli Mawr. He appears in the Mabinogion, the Welsh collection of tales. He owned a cloak of invisibility. The cloak gave him a strong edge in combat. He used it to fight his own cousins and then seized the throne for himself.

okr.objective: Caswallawn is a stealthy Welsh hero who won power through his cloak.
key_results: He is a hero of the Mabinogion.
The variant Caswallan fab Beli Mawr marks his father.
His cloak of invisibility gave him a battle advantage.
He beat his own kin and took the throne.
